name: Yulia Tymoshenko
role: Ukrainian prime minister (2005, 2007-2010); leader of Batkivshchyna
summary: Yulia Tymoshenko is a Ukrainian populist-centrist politician and gas-industry businesswoman who co-led the Orange Revolution. She backs EU and (since 2014) NATO membership and a firm line toward Russia, opposes sale of farmland, and proposes a parliamentary republic with referendums by popular initiative and no immunity for officials. Her programmes combine social insurance and cheap-credit promises with market reforms.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: She said in 2014 that Ukraine 'must be a member of NATO' to protect itself from Russia, which rejects staying out of permanent military alliances.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Her 2014 position is that NATO is the best choice for Ukraine; she wants Ukraine in a bloc, not outside it (she proposed a referendum on NATO versus neutrality, but herself backs NATO).

collective-defense.rationale: She argues for NATO membership as protection against Russian aggression, which is the collective security guarantee the statement describes; she does not discuss Article 5 by name.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: She calls herself a convinced European and states Ukraine's future is in the EU, with a deep free trade agreement leading to candidate status; she does not discuss sovereignty by name.

free-trade.rationale: She backs a free trade area with the EU and WTO entry, saying real competition makes business stronger and modern.

direct-votes.rationale: She repeatedly proposed referendums on major questions (farmland sale, NATO and EU membership, unitary versus federal state) and her programme gives citizens national referendums by popular initiative.

recall-officials.rationale: Her programme gives citizens the undeniable right to change central and local government at any moment through a genuine popular-initiative referendum.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Her programme gives citizens the right to change central and local authorities at any moment through a referendum on popular initiative, which covers recalling elected representatives.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Her programme abolishes the immunity of all high officials: president, judges and deputies.

second-chamber.rationale: In her 2018 speech she proposed a National Assembly of Self-Governance that she likened to an upper house, though the report is secondhand.

decide-locally.rationale: Her programme gives local communities strong rights: their own executive committees, guaranteed taxes in their budgets, and ownership of land outside settlements.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Her programme gives citizens legislative initiative by petition, referendums by popular initiative, elected local judges and community control of land.

right-to-secede.rationale: She warns against separatism in Crimea and Trans-Dniestria and her programme aims to return Crimea and Donbas to Ukraine; she does not address a general right of regions to secede.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Her programme calls Crimea and Donbas occupied territories to be returned; it does not discuss the consent of their inhabitants.

conquest-no-lawful-claim.rationale: She argues Russia must not be allowed to claim ground in former Soviet states by force or secessionist pretexts and her programme seeks the return of occupied Crimea and Donbas.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: She argues Western leaders should speak out against Russia's moves away from democracy and press for free and fair elections there.

suppress-opposition.rationale: She condemns Putin's muzzling of the opposition, and her programme gives parliamentary opposition all rights of parliamentary control.

one-party-rule.rationale: She condemns the Kremlin's drive to monopolize all state power and muzzle opposition, and contrasts it with real democracies.

party-controls-media.rationale: She criticises Russia's government shutting down or taking over newspapers and broadcasters.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: She says amending Russia's constitution to let Putin run again is unacceptable; she did not discuss presidential terms in Ukraine.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: She criticises the Kremlin's desire to curtail the activities of foreign-backed NGOs.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: She argues that without the rule of law the middle class will never gain the confidence a modern economy needs.

no-business-privileges.rationale: She wants to roll back crony capitalism and lawlessness, and her programme abolishes the clan-oligarchic system and 37 quasi-taxes that let officials pressure business.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Her programme introduces compulsory health insurance giving every citizen full services at all levels, with the state paying for children, the unemployed, the disabled and pensioners.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Her programme replaces the current contribution system with personal pension accounts that are state-guaranteed and held in a state bank, so only partly private as the statement says.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Her programme restores one-off birth payments of 50,000, 100,000 and 150,000 hryvnias rising with the child's birth order.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Her programme makes funding of Ukrainian culture and heritage a priority: an inventory and register of architectural monuments, restoration and cultural centres abroad.

widespread-small-property.rationale: She wants 2.5 million farms with cheap loans, makes support of farms and small and medium agrarian firms her main agrarian strategy, and wants farmland sold only to the state.

social-market-economy.rationale: Her programme combines market elements (an electricity market, exchange trading of energy, demonopolised gas imports) with mandatory health insurance and personal pensions.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Her programme has the state develop its own coal industry instead of importing coal and directs Ukrainian-produced gas to households.

traditional-family.rationale: She said the Istanbul Convention would destroy the family values of Ukrainians, which presents traditional family values as worth protecting.
